core.title: Avoid the catalogued artifact-naming anti-patterns
core.given: A plan, product capability, DESIRED OUTCOME, acceptance or doc you author or review declares, uses or references artifact names
core.when: You write, rename, use or review an artifact name
core.then: The artifact name matches none of the catalogued anti-patterns.
prefer: Colons between hierarchy levels; a dot only before a variant
Name only the public artifact; internals stay internal
Only hierarchy levels that add distinction; a specific aspect
avoid: wrong_separator_for_hierarchy: a dot between hierarchy levels instead of a colon; fix: use colons between hierarchy levels
wrong_separator_for_variant: a colon before the variant instead of a dot; fix: use a dot only before the variant
missing_theme: a name with no theme; fix: lead with the theme
too_many_dots: more than one variant segment, encoding internal detail; fix: name only the public artifact, internals stay internal
unnecessary_hierarchy: hierarchy levels that add no distinction; fix: keep only the levels that add distinction
generic_aspect: a vague, generic aspect; fix: make the aspect specific
theme_in_aspect: the theme token repeated inside the aspect; fix: drop the theme token from the aspect
core.why: Artifact names are contract keys between product capabilities; these forms break the theme:aspect.variant grammar, leak internals, or make names vague or duplicative.
evidence: Every artifact name declared, used or referenced in the authored or reviewed planner files matches none of the seven catalogued anti-patterns
For each flagged name, the fix follows the catalogued correction (bad name -> why -> fix)
verification: A check classifies every candidate artifact name extracted from the artifact-name positions of the authored or touched planner files (produce/consume lists, contract keys, artifact references) against the seven catalogued anti-patterns, whether the name is new, renamed or pre-existing.
Extraction must not pre-filter on the theme:aspect[.variant] shape: candidates are taken from artifact-name positions so malformed names (missing theme, wrong separators) are inspected and flagged.
Each flagged name is reported with its catalogued correction in bad name -> why -> fix form.
theme_in_aspect matches when the aspect starts with or contains the theme token.
The check does not cover code identifiers, file names or variable names that are not artifact names, nor work that declares, uses or references no artifact names.

values: artifact name present in authored or touched planner file

fires: Planner declares a new artifact name in a product capability's produce/consume list
Planner renames an artifact in a plan or acceptance
Planner writes a doc or acceptance that uses or references artifact names
Planner reviews a plan containing an existing malformed artifact name
doesNotFire: Planner work that declares, uses or references no artifact names
Code identifiers, file names or variable names that are not artifact names

neutralityNotes: This rule is stack-neutral by construction: it governs the grammar of artifact names inside plan artifacts and names no runtime, framework, language, package manager, suffix or path. 'product capability', 'DESIRED OUTCOME', 'produce/consume' and the theme:aspect[.variant] grammar are ATDD planner methodology vocabulary that the cross-stack profile vocabulary itself carries (layout.capability_dir, urn desired outcome, plan_artifact kinds), so they remain in the core; only the concrete kind list is confirmed through roles.plan_artifact.kinds. The concrete catalogue examples (commons/sensory/match names) are product-specific worked examples with no neutral equivalent; per the neutral-examples rule they are not repeated in the core and remain in bun.json as the delivered reference example (avoid[0..6], verifier_detail[1..7]). Catalogue ids such as too_many_dots reference the reference grammar's dot separator; they are kept unchanged as stable catalogue labels. No severity, disposition, detector id or finding id appears in bun.json, so nothing of that kind had to be moved to bunOnly; activation fires drop only the concrete example name 'gesture.raw'.
